objective: Clean up a bounded area of a codebase without changing behavior: first ask what does not need to exist, then restructure what survives, then independently review the result. Copy this template, replace <scope> with the target paths and <test-command> with the project's real verification suite, and decide isolation per project: run in a linked worktree when the verification commands work there, or set allowInPlaceWrite on R2 when they need the workspace's installed dependencies.

tasks.title: Ask what does not need to exist
tasks.objective: Judge the code under <scope>: what can be deleted or left unwritten, what is already provided by the codebase, the standard library, the platform, or an existing dependency, and what should stay with a stated reason. Never recommend removing validation at a trust boundary, anything preventing data loss, security controls, or accessibility affordances. Your verdict is the work order for the next task — name files and symbols, not vibes.
acceptanceCriteria: Every keep carries a reason; every cut names what already covers it or why it is not needed.
Findings name files and symbols concretely enough to act on.

tasks.title: Restructure what survives
tasks.objective: Apply R1-shrink's verdict to <scope> as behavior-preserving restructuring: delete what it condemned, simplify what it questioned, and reshape what stays — in several small equivalence-preserving steps, not one clever rewrite. Anything that would change a public API, observable behavior, or an error message a caller matches on is not yours to change: report it in unresolvedRisks. Run the named tests fresh and never weaken, skip, or rewrite a test to make the restructuring pass.
acceptanceCriteria: The named test suite passes unmodified.
Every R1 verdict is either applied or reported in unresolvedRisks with a reason.
No public API or observable behavior changed.

tasks.title: Independently review the restructuring
tasks.objective: Review R2-restructure's diff for behavior changes that slipped through: altered edge-case handling, error paths, ordering, or resource lifetimes. When filling this template, set allowedProviders to the provider the dry run did NOT give R2-restructure. Confirm or refute against the code, not against R2's receipt.
acceptanceCriteria: Each suspected behavior change is confirmed or refuted against the code.
The verdict states plainly whether the diff is behavior-preserving.
